lines.text: What if the Sun vanished? How soon would you know?
lines.phonemes: wˌʌt ɪf ðə sˈʌn vˈænɪʃt? hˌaʊ sˈuːn wʊd juː nˈoʊ?

lines.text: Rewind. We circle the Sun at nearly thirty kilometers a second. It's so far away that even its light needs eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach us.
lines.phonemes: ɹᵻwˈaɪnd. wiː sˈɜːkəl ðə sˈʌn æt nˌɪɹli θˈɜːɾi kˈɪləmˌiːɾɚz ɐ sˈɛkənd. ɪts sˈoʊ fˌɑːɹ ɐwˈeɪ ðæt ˈiːvən ɪts lˈaɪt nˈiːdz ˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts ænd twˈɛnti sˈɛkəndz tə ɹˈiːtʃ ˌʌs.

lines.text: Now switch it off. Down here, nothing changes. Its last light is on the way: for over eight minutes, your sky looks exactly the same.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ swˈɪtʃ ɪɾ ˈɔf. dˌaʊn hˈɪɹ, nˈʌθɪŋ tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz. ɪts lˈæst lˈaɪt ɪz ɔnðə wˈeɪ: fɔːɹ ˌoʊvɚɹ ˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts, jʊɹ skˈaɪ lˈʊks ɛɡzˈæktli ðə sˈeɪm.

lines.text: Gravity is no faster: changes in it travel at the speed of light. In twenty seventeen, we caught two neutron stars colliding. Their light and gravitational waves crossed a hundred and thirty million light-years, and arrived under two seconds apart.
lines.phonemes: ɡɹˈævᵻɾi ɪz nˈoʊ fˈæstɚ: tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz ɪn ɪt tɹˈævəl æt ðə spˈiːd ʌv lˈaɪt. ɪn twˈɛnti sˈɛvəntˌiːn, wiː kˈɔːt tˈuː nˈuːtɹɑːn stˈɑːɹz kəlˈaɪdɪŋ. ðɛɹ lˈaɪt ænd ɡɹˌævɪtˈeɪʃənəl wˈeɪvz kɹˈɔst ɐ hˈʌndɹɪd ænd θˈɜːɾi mˈɪliən lˈaɪtjˈɪɹz, ænd ɚɹˈaɪvd ˌʌndɚ tˈuː sˈɛkəndz ɐpˈɑːɹt.

lines.text: So for eight minutes, Earth keeps circling a Sun that isn't there. Then the news arrives, and Earth sails off, straight into the dark.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ fɔːɹ ˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts, ˈɜːθ kˈiːps sˈɜːklɪŋ ɐ sˈʌn ðæt ˌɪzənt ðˈɛɹ. ðˈɛn ðə nˈuːz ɚɹˈaɪvz, ænd ˈɜːθ sˈeɪlz ˈɔf, stɹˈeɪt ˌɪntʊ ðə dˈɑːɹk.

lines.text: Light and gravity share one speed limit. Everything you see in the sky is old news.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt ænd ɡɹˈævᵻɾi ʃˈɛɹ wˈʌn spˈiːd lˈɪmɪt. ˈɛvɹɪθˌɪŋ juː sˈiː ɪnðə skˈaɪ ɪz ˈoʊld nˈuːz.

lines.text: Light time, Sun to Earth: eight minutes, twenty seconds. Our galaxy's center: light from the last Ice Age.
lines.phonemes: lˈaɪt tˈaɪm, sˈʌn tʊ ˈɜːθ: ˈeɪt mˈɪnɪts, twˈɛnti sˈɛkəndz. ˌaʊɚ ɡˈælɐksiz sˈɛntɚ: lˈaɪt fɹʌmðə lˈæst ˈaɪs ˈeɪdʒ.

lines.text: Next: leave for the nearest star today. When do we arrive?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: lˈiːv fɚðə nˌɪɹɪst stˈɑːɹ tədˈeɪ. wˌɛn dˈuː wiː ɚɹˈaɪv?
